InformationTheory.use: Solve numericals on paper, do not just reread

Rotation.use: Java, Computer Organization (CO) or Probability, as listed

RecallBuffer.use: Closed-book redo of yesterday's topic, 3 numericals or 1 handwritten program, then catch up on anything missed

recallRules.description: Active recall: redo yesterday's topic closed-book, then again about 3 days later and a week later.

intervals.description: Recall again about a week later

recallRules.conflictRule: If a recall date falls on an exam day or unavailable day, flag it for review — do not silently move it.
recallRules.numericalRecall: Solve at least 3 problems on paper per numerical recall.
recallRules.programRecall: Write at least 1 handwritten program per program recall.

catchUpRules: Then reduce detail in Priority 3 topics.
Never cut the next exam's practice.
Never cut Information Theory numericals before 2 December.
Never cut Probability test and ANOVA practice.
If two consecutive days slip, drop low-priority topics at once rather than trying to repay every missed hour.
